scheme_name: Marriage Grant for the Marriage of Daughters of Widows of Ex-servicemen (other than War Widows)
description:
The Marriage Grant for the Marriage of Daughters of Widows of Ex-servicemen is a specific welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India. 

This scheme was launched to provide financial assistance to the daughters of widows of ex-servicemen who are not classified as war widows. 

The scheme aims to alleviate the financial burden associated with the marriage of daughters in families that have lost their primary breadwinner due to military service. 

The initiative recognizes the unique challenges faced by these families and provides targeted support to help ensure that daughters can have a dignified marriage. 

The scheme was officially launched in the year 2006. 

Since its inception, the Marriage Grant has been instrumental in supporting numerous families across the country. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide a one-time financial grant to assist with the marriage expenses of eligible daughters. 

The specific goal is to empower widows of ex-servicemen by ensuring that their daughters can marry without the added stress of financial constraints. 

The grant amount provided under this scheme is ₹30,000. 

This amount is intended to cover various expenses related to the marriage ceremony, including but not limited to, venue costs, catering, and other associated expenses. 

Eligible beneficiaries must meet specific criteria to qualify for the grant. 

The applicant must be a widow of an ex-serviceman. 

The ex-serviceman must not have been classified as a war widow. 

The daughter for whom the grant is being sought must be unmarried at the time of application. 

There is no specific age limit mentioned for the daughter; however, the marriage must take place within a reasonable timeframe after the grant is received. 

Income criteria are also specified for eligibility. 

The family income of the widow must not exceed ₹1,50,000 per annum. 

This income limit ensures that the grant is directed towards those who are in genuine need of financial assistance. 

The application process for the Marriage Grant is straightforward but requires specific documentation. 

Applicants must fill out the prescribed application form, which can be obtained from the local office of the Directorate of Sainik Welfare or online through the official government portal. 

Along with the application form, the following documents must be submitted: 

A copy of the death certificate of the ex-serviceman. 

Proof of the widow's identity, such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Proof of income, which can be a salary slip, income certificate, or any other relevant document. 

A copy of the daughter’s birth certificate or any document proving her age. 

The application must be submitted to the local office of the Directorate of Sainik Welfare in the respective state. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The processing time for the application can vary but generally takes about 30 to 45 days. 

If approved, the grant amount of ₹30,000 is disbursed directly to the bank account of the widow. 

The disbursement is typically made in a single installment. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. 

The Directorate of Sainik Welfare in each state is responsible for the execution of the scheme at the state level. 

Contact details for the Directorate of Sainik Welfare can be found on the official Ministry of Defence website. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to support ex-servicemen and their families. 

It reflects the government's commitment to the welfare of those who have served the nation. 

The Marriage Grant is not only a financial assistance program but also a recognition of the sacrifices made by ex-servicemen and their families. 

As of the latest updates, the scheme has benefited thousands of families since its launch. 

The government has made efforts to raise awareness about the scheme to ensure that eligible beneficiaries are informed. 

Workshops and outreach programs have been conducted to educate widows about the application process and eligibility criteria. 

The scheme has been positively received by the community, with many beneficiaries expressing gratitude for the financial support. 

In addition to the Marriage Grant, the government offers various other welfare schemes for ex-servicemen and their families. 

These include pension schemes, educational scholarships, and employment assistance programs. 

The Marriage Grant specifically addresses the unique challenges faced by widows of ex-servicemen. 

It aims to promote social inclusion and support the dignity of families in need. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the process and address any challenges faced during application. 

The Marriage Grant for the Marriage of Daughters of Widows of Ex-servicemen is an essential component of India's welfare initiatives. 

It serves as a crucial support mechanism for families navigating the complexities of marriage in the absence of a husband. 

The financial assistance provided through this scheme is a step towards ensuring that no daughter of a widow of an ex-serviceman is deprived of a dignified marriage due to financial constraints. 

Overall, the scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the welfare of ex-servicemen and their families. 

It highlights the importance of targeted assistance in addressing the specific needs of vulnerable populations. 

As the scheme continues to evolve, it remains a vital resource for those it aims to serve. 

The Marriage Grant is a clear example of how government initiatives can make a tangible difference in the lives of citizens. 

In conclusion, the Marriage Grant for the Marriage of Daughters of Widows of Ex-servicemen is a significant welfare scheme that provides essential financial support. 

It empowers widows and their daughters by alleviating the financial burden associated with marriage. 

The scheme is a crucial part of India's broader commitment to supporting its veterans and their families.
